</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 83

<row gap="medium">
**Ammunition** any

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The body of a _weapon shot_ is translucent and filled with quicksilver. It imparts its magic to the weapon used to fire it or it summons a translucent weapon, made of force, to fire it. It's a favorite of killers and sharpshooters who need just one shot in a situation where carrying ammunition is easier than carrying a weapon.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))    **Effect** For the Strike with which you consume the ammunition, use the ammunition's fundamental runes, according to its type, instead of those of the weapon firing it.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** A ghostly weapon made of force appears, wielded by you and loaded with the _weapon shot_ you activated. The conjured weapon sublimates into motes of briefly luminous dust if the _weapon shot_ deactivates without you using it or just after you use the activated shot. For the Strike with which it functions, the weapon uses the ammunition's fundamental runes, according to its type.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

>
[Weapon Shot](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2059)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 83

<row gap="medium">
**Ammunition** any

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The body of a _weapon shot_ is translucent and filled with quicksilver. It imparts its magic to the weapon used to fire it or it summons a translucent weapon, made of force, to fire it. It's a favorite of killers and sharpshooters who need just one shot in a situation where carrying ammunition is easier than carrying a weapon.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))    **Effect** For the Strike with which you consume the ammunition, use the ammunition's fundamental runes, according to its type, instead of those of the weapon firing it.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** A ghostly weapon made of force appears, wielded by you and loaded with the _weapon shot_ you activated. The conjured weapon sublimates into motes of briefly luminous dust if the _weapon shot_ deactivates without you using it or just after you use the activated shot. For the Strike with which it functions, the weapon uses the ammunition's fundamental runes, according to its type.

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Weapon Siphon](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1987)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Adjustment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=380" />
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 65

**Price** 10 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** attached to a melee weapon

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This set of tubing snakes down the striking surface of a weapon to deliver alchemical explosives. A single lesser alchemical bomb can be fitted to the weapon siphon as an Interact action. The bomb must be one that deals energy damage, such as an [acid flask](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3286), [alchemist’s fire](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3287), [blasting stone](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3288), [bottled lightning](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3290), or [frost vial](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3293). The next three attacks made with the weapon deal 1d4 damage of the bomb’s damage type in addition to the weapon’s normal damage. If the second and third attacks aren’t all made within 1 minute of the first attack, the bomb’s energy is wasted. These attacks never deal splash damage or other special effects of the bomb and aren’t modified by any abilities that add to or modify a bomb’s effect.

Adding a weapon siphon to a weapon throws off its balance, causing the multiple attack penalty with the weapon to be one greater than usual (usually –6 on a second attack and –11 on a third; or –5 and –10 with an agile weapon).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</row>

</row>

</column>

---

Each dose of _weapon-weird oil_ is keyed to a particular melee weapon group, selected from among [axe](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=1), [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4), [club](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=5), [flail](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=7), [hammer](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=8), [knife](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=9), [pick](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=10), [polearm](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=11), [shield](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=12), [spear](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=14), and [sword](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=15). The oil creates a synergy between skill and weapon, enabling you to wield the weapon in unexpected ways. You must have proficiency with the original weapon to benefit from the oil; however, you use your proficiency rank with the oil's keyed group instead of the weapon's original group. Also, you apply the [critical specialization effect](/Rules.aspx?ID=235) from the oil's keyed group instead of the weapon's normal critical specialization effect. [What Doors We Open](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3705)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Spore War</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Grimoire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=387" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #211: The Secret of Deathstalk Tower](/Sources.aspx?ID=254) pg. 83

**Price** 4,500 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

_What Doors We Open_ is the culmination of Aravashnial’s research. Before he was captured, he performed a 1-minute ritual to erase his spells from this book and then hid it at his campsite to prevent his [demonic](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=387) foes from learning too many of his secrets. A spellcaster can transfer their own spells to this grimoire using a similar 1-minute ritual. When a spellcaster prepares their spells from it, they gain the ability to Activate the grimoire until their next [daily preparations](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575) and gain a +2 item bonus to checks made to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) about demons. A grimoire’s benefits apply only to spells cast via spell slots. No one can use more than one grimoire per day, nor can a grimoire be used by more than one person per day.

**Activate—Cast Out** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** If the next activity you take this round is to cast [_banishment_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1448) prepared from this grimoire, it counts as the extra cost of adding an object that is anathema to the creature and gives the creature a –2 circumstance penalty to its save. If the targeted creature is a [demon](/Traits.aspx?ID=573), increase this to a –3 circumstance penalty.

**Activate—Open the Door Within** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** The inside back cover of _What Doors We Open_ features a realistic depiction of a bejeweled door set in a stone wall. When you Open the Door Within, you open that door to reveal an extradimensional space that otherwise functions identically to a [type II spacious pouch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3032).

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 0"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Wheelbarrow](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1404)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 93

**Price** 5 sp

<row gap="medium">

**Hands** 2

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 5
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This small, hand-propelled vehicle has a single wheel and is designed to carry large loads over a distance. A wheelbarrow can typically hold up to 5 Bulk of objects without issue. The GM might rule that it can hold more Bulk of particular items, such as sand, or less Bulk of other items, like awkwardly shaped rocks.

 You can raise or place a wheelbarrow using an Interact action and can Stride your normal Speed while you have the wheelbarrow raised, though you're [encumbered](/Conditions.aspx?ID=12) while pushing a wheelbarrow. You can Release a wheelbarrow as normal, but a loaded wheelbarrow has a chance of tipping over if you don't place it down with care. When you Release a wheelbarrow, attempt a DC 7 flat check. On a failure, the wheelbarrow tips over, spilling its contents into a randomly determined adjacent space.

>
[Whip of Compliance](/Equipment.aspx?ID=593)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Extinction Curse</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #152: Legacy of the Lost God](/Sources.aspx?ID=23) pg. 75

**Price** 3,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held, 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Whip](/Weapons.aspx?ID=48)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The handle of this braided leather _+1 striking [whip](/Weapons.aspx?ID=48)_ is made from the hairs of a variety of rare and mythical animals. When used against an animal, the _whip of compliance_ can potentially force the target to follow your commands.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command;     **Effect** Until the end of your current turn, any animals you Strike with the whip must attempt a DC 25 Will save. On a failed or critically failed saving throw, the whip casts a 4th-level [_suggestion_](/Spells.aspx?ID=315) spell on the animal with a base duration of 1 round, and the spell loses the [linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=101) trait. The course of action must still fulfill _suggestion’s_ requirements. If you can cast spells, you can expend one of your spells of 4th level or higher as a part of activating the whip; if you do so, the _suggestions_ this turn have their normal base duration.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

>
[Whip-Tongue Sling](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3213)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 104

**Price** 1,250 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Sling](/Weapons.aspx?ID=430)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This is a _[+2](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2830) [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) [sling](/Weapons.aspx?ID=430)_ made from the neck, jaw, and tongue of a [mobogo](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1229) to resemble its mouth. The tongue curls around each bullet, which is thrown with the snap of your wrist. Each throw causes a small croak to echo from the sling.

**Activate—Bolstering Croak** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You raise your sling and work the handle to mimic a mobogo’s croaking song. Allies within 25 feet gain a +1 status bonus to saves against [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598) effects for 1 round. You can [Sustain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) this for up to 4 rounds. During this time, you can’t use the sling to [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) or activate its Tongue Twister ability. After using Bolstering Croak, you can recharge it once per day by feeding the sling a number of gallons of water equal to double the number of rounds for which the Bolstering Croak was active. For example, if you activated but didn’t sustain Bolstering Croak, you would require 2 gallons of water to recharge it. If you activated Bolstering Cloak and then Sustained for 1 round, you would require 4 gallons of water.

**Activate—Tongue Twister** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))   **Requirements** The sling isn’t loaded; **Effect** You fully unfurl the sling’s tongue to grab hold of a creature within 20 feet, and attempt to move them. Attempt an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) check against the creature’s Fortitude DC. On a success, you can move the creature up to 15 feet into any space within 20 feet of you. If you target a willing ally with this ability, you automatically succeed at the Athletics check.

**Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include the throat, tongue, and skin from a [mobogo](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1229).

**Price** 55 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** affixed to armor or to an outfit if a character has no armor

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Two Actions" /><row>envision</row></row>

 

 

**Requirement** You are an expert in [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15).
</row>

</column>

---

This teardrop-shaped gemstone has triangular facets and looks suitable for fancy attire, although close inspection shows that it's hollow. When it's activated, you can instantly impart up to 1 minute of speech (roughly 150 words) telepathically to any creatures you choose within 100 feet. You can impart this instantaneous telepathic message to creatures that you perceive and creatures hidden to you, but you can't do so to undetected creatures. Once used, the _whisper briolette_ becomes unusable and subtly vanishes within the next few minutes, rather than crumbling to dust.

<traits>

<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 297

**Price** 60,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This delicate necklace contains bottled whispers distilled from a source on the Astral Plane rumored to be connected to the first lie ever told. While wearing the necklace, you gain a +3 item bonus to Deception checks, and you can attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) effects that would force you to tell the truth or determine whether you are lying. Success on this counteract attempt lets you ignore the effect, rather than removing the effect entirely. The counteract rank is 9, with a counteract modifier of +35. 

**Activate—Release the Lie** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))    **Effect** You unstopper the vial and release the lie, creating the effect of a [_fabricated truth_](/Spells.aspx?ID=106) (DC 47). The vial is emptied and can never be activated again.

**Craft Requirements** Supply a casting of _fabricated truth_.

</column>

May contain spoilers from Bastion of Blasphemies **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 236 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** L --- When dislodged, mortal fragments like a chewed fingernail, a careless sneeze, or a few strands of hair might fall to the soil and be swiftly forgotten. When a horror like Charg brushes close to reality, the _vile remnants_ cast off from his nightmare form are not so harmless. At other times, the desecrated remains of innocent creatures can be transformed into _vile remnants_ as well. Worshippers of unholy gods and followers of evil philosophies gather these things and covet them as one might the hem of a cloak brushed against an idolized hero, or the visage of a divinity made manifest in a patch of mold on a wall. _Vile remnants_ spread fear and cruelty wherever they’re [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) and can corrupt those who discover them. They might be buried in the soil of a farmer’s field, dropped into the depths of a village well, or stashed at the bottom of a toy box. Wherever the innocent might stumble across them and become unknowing actors in the decay of morality, the _vile remnant_ works its unholy magic. A _vile remnant_ appears as a raw, decaying mass of flesh, fur, and gristle—a teratoma consisting of warty skin, sightless eyes, a finger or a toe, tufts of bristly hair, or teeth without mouths or lips to hide them. Each _vile remnant’s_ shape is wildly different and uniquely unsettling. A _vile remnant_ automatically imparts to a PC the knowledge of how to use its Hear My Words activation as soon as it’s touched, but its other activations must be discovered normally through the use of Identify Magic (and as normal, identifying the presence and effect of the curse it carries requires a critical success at such an attempt). Unlike most cursed items, a character can discard a _vile remnant_, yet doing so runs a real risk that it might thereafter fall into the wrong hands. In this Adventure Path, any _vile remnant_ the PCs discard anywhere other than the restored reliquary in the Maiserene Church at area **A9** is discovered by one of the monsters of Bastardhall, who then [Hides](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404) the horror somewhere in the region where it was found. Where the horror is hidden is left to you to decide. As long as a creature carries a _vile remnant_, its thoughts and dreams are influenced by cruel notions and temptations to commit violent depravities. A creature that’s already predisposed toward these acts derives greater pleasure than before for such atrocities but receives no additional penalty or benefit, while a non-sapient creature is driven to become unnaturally violent in its actions (and over the course of weeks, becomes visibly corrupted by patches of strange fur, warty growths, unsightly teeth, or similar teratomas on its body). A sapient creature that isn’t predisposed toward acts of depravity (likely including all PCs) takes an item penalty equal to the number of _vile remnants_ they carry to saving throws against all magical effects that attempt to encourage such acts. Saving throws against spells like _suggestion_ or _charm_ cast by creatures who attempt to push a PC into such acts, any affect by such creatures that attempts to control a PC, or certain specific effects mentioned in the text of this adventure would all be affected by this penalty. A creature with the [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) trait reduces the overall item penalty imparted by this curse by 1, to a minimum penalty of 0. A creature that’s foolish enough to consume a _vile remnant_ becomes fused to its curse, at which point the _vile remnant_ remains lodged within the creature’s body until the curse is removed from the creature with a _cleanse affliction_ spell or similar magic, or upon the creature’s death, whichever comes first. At this point, the _vile remnant_ crawls or oozes its way out of the creature’s body and flops, once again inanimate, onto the ground, where it waits to be claimed by a new carrier. As long as you carry a _vile remnant_ somewhere on your person, its curse does have a beneficial side: The power of its influence grants you a +1 item bonus to all saving throws against curses from other sources, as the _vile remnant_ jealously wards against such encroachments on its territory. Unlike the item penalty, carrying multiple _vile remnants_ does not increase this item bonus. The base version of a _vile remnant_ appears to be lifeless, but the _whispering remnant_ periodically twitches and pulses as if it were alive. **Activate—Become As One** 1 minute ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Effect** By piling eight _vile remnants_ in a heap and then concentrating upon the mound of cursed flesh for a minute, you cause the eight _vile remnants_ to slither together and become a single _whispering remnant_. Once combined in this manner, the resulting _whispering remnant_ cannot be thereafter split into individual _vile remnants_. **Activate—Hear My Words** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** The _vile remnant_ casts a DC 23 _enthrall_ spell to your specifications. Creatures that fail or critically fail to resist this spell perceive and remember the _vile remnant_ in your hand as something commonplace to the region, such as a farming tool, book, or fresh-baked pie, for as long as they remain enthralled. If you don’t take advantage of this to subtly guide any affected creatures toward undermining their society, the _vile remnant_ can’t be activated to Hear My Words again by you for 1 week. Additionally, the next time you sleep, you endure horrific nightmares and must succeed at a DC 23 Will save upon waking to avoid becoming [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1 for 24 hours (this is a mental effect). **Activate—Hide the Horror** 10 minutes ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per year; **Effect** You hide the _vile remnant_ somewhere that, in time, it is likely to be found. For the following four weeks, _the vile remnant_’s evil seeps into the surrounding landscape, expanding its influence at a rate of 200 feet per day until it reaches its maximum emanation of 5,600 feet after 28 days. It continues to influence this area for another three weeks before going dormant— it must be recovered and rehidden later once this activation recharges to begin the cycle again. While the remnant’s influence is active, any sapient creature that sleeps in the area experiences unsettling dreams of being stalked by monsters they can never quite see or evade. A creature that doesn’t worship an unholy deity who experiences these dreams must succeed at a DC 23 Will save each time they rest to avoid awakening [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=73). On a critical failure, the creature awakens [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1 as well; this condition remains until removed or until they are no longer fatigued, whichever comes first. Creatures who worship an unholy deity or follow a despicable philosophy are immune to this effect. Any skill checks made by such creatures when performing rituals performed in the affected area gain a +1 item bonus, and _nightmare_ spells cast by them within the region have their save DCs increased by 1. **Destruction** A _vile remnant_ can’t be destroyed, but a _whispering remnant_ can be by hurling it into a powerful curse effect created by the deity associated with the remnant. This causes the _whispering remnant_ to become reabsorbed into the deity’s otherworldly body and often has potent side effects on the surrounding region. Disposing of a _whispering remnant_ in the soul vortex of Bastardhall (area
**I**) after Caydserris has been defeated not only destroys the _whispering remnant_ but helps bring the Bastardhall Curse to an end. Vile Remnant **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 238 **Bulk** L Whispering Remnant **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 238 **Bulk** L --- A _whispering remnant’s_ Hide the Horror aura expands at a rate of 500 feet per day for 28 days, and the DC’s for its Hear My Words and [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404) the Horror activations increase to 30. It imparts a -9 item penalty to all saving throws against deplorable influences and a +3 item bonus to all saving throws against curses as long as it’s carried. _Whispering remnants_ are incredibly rare, and their use is required in many vile rites, such as the one that brought down the curse on Castle Arudora. A _whispering remnant_ gains the following additional activation. **Activate—Heed My Whispers** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** The _whispering remnant_ casts a DC 30 [_subconscious suggestion_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1692) spell to your specifications. If the target of the spell fails or critically fails to save against this, they perceive and remember the _whispering remnant_ as being a commonplace item. If you don’t suggest a course of action to the target that causes them to work at undermining their society, the _whispering remnant_ shrieks horribly, but only in your mind—you take 10d6 mental damage (DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Will save), after which the _whispering remnant_ cannot be activated again by you for 1 week.

A creature that doesn’t worship an unholy deity who experiences these dreams must succeed at a DC 23 Will save each time they rest to avoid awakening fatigued. On a critical failure, the creature awakens stupefied 1 as well; this condition remains until removed or until they are no longer fatigued, whichever comes first. Creatures who worship an unholy deity or follow a despicable philosophy are immune to this effect. Any skill checks made by such creatures when performing rituals performed in the affected area gain a +1 item bonus, and nightmare spells cast by them within the region have their save DCs increased by 1. Destruction A vile remnant can’t be destroyed, but a whispering remnant can be by hurling it into a powerful curse effect created by the deity associated with the remnant. This causes the whispering remnant to become reabsorbed into the deity’s otherworldly body and often has potent side effects on the surrounding region. Disposing of a whispering remnant in the soul vortex of Bastardhall (area I ) after Caydserris has been defeated not only destroys the whispering remnant but helps bring the Bastardhall Curse to an end. Item 7 Vile Remnant Source Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies pg. 238 Bulk L Item 13 Whispering Remnant Source Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies pg. 238 Bulk L A whispering remnant’s Hide the Horror aura expands at a rate of 500 feet per day for 28 days, and the DC’s for its Hear My Words and Hide the Horror activations increase to 30. It imparts a -9 item penalty to all saving throws against deplorable influences and a +3 item bonus to all saving throws against curses as long as it’s carried. Whispering remnants are incredibly rare, and their use is required in many vile rites, such as the one that brought down the curse on Castle Arudora. A whispering remnant gains the following additional activation. Activate—Heed My Whispers Two Actions (concentrate, manipulate) Frequency once per day; Effect The whispering remnant casts a DC 30 subconscious suggestion spell to your specifications. If the target of the spell fails or critically fails to save against this, they perceive and remember the whispering remnant as being a commonplace item. If you don’t suggest a course of action to the target that causes them to work at undermining their society, the whispering remnant shrieks horribly, but only in your mind—you take 10d6 mental damage (DC 30 basic Will save), after which the whispering remnant cannot be activated again by you for 1 week.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Staff" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=151" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 105

**Price** 70,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This gnarled wooden staff is carved with humanoid faces in various emotional states. When the staff is activated, the faces begin to whisper a variety of languages in sibilant tones, creating what seems to be nonsense to all but the staff's wielder or those they choose to affect. The staff functions as a [_major staff of the unblinking eye_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3048). While using the staff, you gain a +3 item bonus to [Decipher Writing](/Actions.aspx?ID=22), [Identify Magic](/Actions.aspx?ID=24), and [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) checks, regardless of the skill. When you invest the staff, you either increase your Intelligence modifier by 1 or increase it to +4, whichever would give you a higher value. You must select the skills and languages the first time you invest the item, and whenever you invest the same _whispering staff_, you get the same skills and languages you chose the first time.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Frequency** once per round;   **Effect** Through the staff's strange whispering, you gain a glimpse into the mind and desires of one creature you can see within 30 feet. Until the end of your next turn, that creature is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) to you and takes a –2 circumstance penalty to saving throws against your spells.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=654)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You point the staff at one creature you can see within 30 feet of you, causing the whispers to howl in that creature's mind. The target must attempt a DC 43 Will save. If it fails, whenever the creature attempts an attack roll, skill check, or saving throw, it must roll twice and take the worse roll. This lasts until the start of your next turn.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You twirl the staff in three consecutive circles and call for the whispers to speak up. For the next minute, you and all allies within a 30-foot emanation around you can hear your staff's whispers clearly and distinctly, gaining benefit from their advice and mental protection. Whenever you and your affected allies attempt to Recall Knowledge or attempt a saving throw against a [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) effect, you roll twice and take the better result. This is a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76) effect.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [High Seas](/Sources.aspx?ID=351) pg. 78

**Price** 2,600 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn mask

**Bulk** L
</row>

**Access** You're from the Mordant Spire

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Carved concentric circles surround the eye and ear holes on this dark wooden mask, which lets you hear the whispers that fill the Mordant Spire. The barely audible susurrus that fills your ears advises you of peril, granting you a +1 item bonus to Perception checks for initiative and to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301), [Search](/Actions.aspx?ID=2630), or [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=2302) against things that intend harm to you, at the GM’s discretion, such as hostile creatures and haunts. If you tie a foe’s initiative roll, you go first. 

**Activate—Spire Power** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You are about to attempt a check that your mythic calling would allow you to spend a Mythic Point on;  **Effect** You draw on the power of the Mordant Spire. You gain 1 Mythic Point, which you can spend to attempt the check. If you don’t spend this point by the end of this turn, it is lost. You do not regain a Mythic Point if you critically succeed on the check, even if it’s the first time you did so that day, but still do so on the subsequent critical success, as usual. 

**Activate—Unforeseen Alert** <actions string="Free Action" /> ;    **Requirements** A creature or hazard you aren’t aware of targets you or includes you in an area effect, and you aren’t [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=66); **Effect** The whispers warn you of the impending danger. You immediately gain a reaction that you can use only to respond to the triggering action or effect.

</column>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Knights of Lastwall](/Sources.aspx?ID=123) pg. 91

**Price** 6,300 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

**Access** Knights of Lastwall have access to this item.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A _whistle of calling_ appears to be a simple brass whistle. It changes slightly in appearance depending on the type of creature to which it's attuned, depicting small carvings of hooves, feather patterns, claws, or other appropriate motifs.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes (Interact);     **Effect** You blow the whistle at different tones in the presence of a companion or another allied creature willing to be your mount. At the end of the 10 minutes, the whistle is attuned to that creature. The whistle can be attuned to only one creature at any time, but you can attune it to a new one with another 10-minute activation.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You blow the whistle and the creature to which it is attuned teleports instantly from as far as 1 mile away to an unoccupied space within 30 feet of you. The whistle has no effect if the attuned creature is dead, on another plane, or outside the range.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Curtain Call</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #206: Bring the House Down](/Sources.aspx?ID=247) pg. 83

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn eyepiece

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Delicate engravings of spiders and cleomes decorate the silver cover of this magnifying loupe. _White Cleome’s Eye_ functions as [_spectacles of inquiry_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2316), but the item bonuses granted to [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=2298) checks increase by 1 (so +3 while worn, and +4 to [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=2302) when you activate the artifact).

Once restored, _White Cleome’s Eye_ gains the following additional activations.

**Activate—Look to the Past** <actions string="" /> 1 minute ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You twist _White Cleome’s Eye_ in a clockwise rotation, allowing you to peer back in time, causing it to cast a 9th-rank [_retrocognition_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1652) spell.

**Activate—Relive the Past** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You twist _White Cleome’s Eye_ in a counter-clockwise rotation, allowing you to experience previous events that impacted an object you are touching, causing _White Cleome’s Eye_ to cast a 9th-rank [_object reading_](/Spells.aspx?ID=2012) spell.

</column>

**Price** 45 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn headwear

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

_Wigs of holding_ are created from planar fibers and contain small extradimensional spaces accessible within the hair. They can hold up to four items of light Bulk inside them, and Bulk held within the _wig of holding_ doesn't increase the Bulk of the wig itself. You can Interact with a _wig of holding_ to put items inside or remove items from it, and you can do so more easily than with a mundane container. It only takes a single Interact action to withdraw these items, like a worn item, rather than taking two Interact actions, like a stowed item.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Tattoo" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=262" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 123

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** tattooed on the body

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These curving, delicate designs resemble leaves, vines, or creepers, most often wrapped around a limb, ear, or throat, or curled around specific muscles. They help you blend in among plants. You gain a +1 item bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks, which increases to +2 in forests.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** A creature would detect you by [Seeking](/Actions.aspx?ID=84); **Requirements** You're in a forest or similar natural area; **Effect** The tattoo casts [_one with plants_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1618) to turn you into a plant before you can be noticed. The duration of this spell is 10 minutes. 

If you’ve already Activated the tattoo, you can supply a separate casting of _one with plants_ to recharge the tattoo instead of having the spell’s normal effect. This allows you to Activate the tattoo again in the same day. You can do so multiple times each day, but only as many times as you continue to cast one with plants to recharge the tattoo after each use.

fields.text: Item 4+ Wildwood Ink Invested Primal Tattoo Source Treasure Vault (Remastered) pg. 123 Usage tattooed on the body These curving, delicate designs resemble leaves, vines, or creepers, most often wrapped around a limb, ear, or throat, or curled around specific muscles. They help you blend in among plants. You gain a +1 item bonus to Stealth checks, which increases to +2 in forests. Activate Reaction (concentrate) Frequency once per day; Trigger A creature would detect you by Seeking; Requirements You're in a forest or similar natural area; Effect The tattoo casts one with plants to turn you into a plant before you can be noticed. The duration of this spell is 10 minutes. If you’ve already Activated the tattoo, you can supply a separate casting of one with plants to recharge the tattoo instead of having the spell’s normal effect. This allows you to Activate the tattoo again in the same day. You can do so multiple times each day, but only as many times as you continue to cast one with plants to recharge the tattoo after each use. Item 4 Wildwood Ink Source Treasure Vault (Remastered) pg. 123 Price 80 gp Item 10 Wildwood Ink (Greater) Source Treasure Vault (Remastered) pg. 123 Price 900 gp The item bonus to Stealth checks is +2, or +3 in forests. One with plants lasts up to 1 hour. Item 17 Wildwood Ink (Major) Source Treasure Vault (Remastered) pg. 123 Price 15,000 gp The item bonus to Stealth checks is +3, or +4 in forests. One with plants lasts up to 8 hours.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 4+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Wildwood Ink](/Equipment.aspx?ID=4758)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
<trait label="Tattoo" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=262" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=320) pg. 123

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** tattooed on the body

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These curving, delicate designs resemble leaves, vines, or creepers, most often wrapped around a limb, ear, or throat, or curled around specific muscles. They help you blend in among plants. You gain a +1 item bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) checks, which increases to +2 in forests.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ;  **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** A creature would detect you by Seeking; **Requirements** You’re in a forest or similar natural area; **Effect** The tattoo casts tree shape on you before you can be noticed. The duration of this spell is 10 minutes.

If you’ve already Activated the tattoo, you can supply a separate casting of [_tree shape_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1618) to recharge the tattoo instead of having the spell’s normal effect. This allows you to Activate the tattoo again in the same day. You can do so multiple times each day, but only as many times as you continue to cast tree shape to recharge the tattoo after each use.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---

These curving, delicate designs resemble leaves, vines, or creepers, most often wrapped around a limb, ear, or throat, or curled around specific muscles. They help you blend in among plants. You gain a +1 item bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) checks, which increases to +2 in forests.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ;  **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** A creature would detect you by Seeking; **Requirements** You’re in a forest or similar natural area; **Effect** The tattoo casts tree shape on you before you can be noticed. The duration of this spell is 10 minutes.

If you’ve already Activated the tattoo, you can supply a separate casting of [_tree shape_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1618) to recharge the tattoo instead of having the spell’s normal effect. This allows you to Activate the tattoo again in the same day. You can do so multiple times each day, but only as many times as you continue to cast tree shape to recharge the tattoo after each use.

>
[Wind at Your Back](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2201)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Air" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=5" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 117

**Price** 130 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This object can only be described as a gray, solidified, miniature cloud that feels spongy to the touch. The cloud is incredibly soft and can be easily lifted with little effort, though its ephemeral nature requires using two hands to ensure it doesn't slip from your grasp.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You blow across the surface of the cloud, and it floats free of you and calls up a strong breeze. For the next 8 hours, it floats behind you and your companions, increasing the amount of time the group can [Hustle](/Actions.aspx?ID=515) during exploration to the lowest Constitution modifier in the group × 20 instead of × 10. You must all remain within 100 feet to get the benefit.

 If you activate the item aboard a vehicle, you instead grant the vehicle a +10-foot circumstance bonus to its Speeds for 8 hours. If the vehicle is powered by wind, such as a sailing ship, the bonus increases to +20 feet.

 When the 8 hours are up, the cloud stops blowing and floats back into your hands.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 99 **Price** 50 gp **Usage** held in 2 hands **Bulk** L **Activate**([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) --- A blue finish decorates the ceramic body of a _wind ocarina_. When you play a note on this ocarina, for 1 minute, winds sweep into strong gusts in a 5-foot emanation around you. The winds have the following effects.
  • Ammunition from physical ranged attacks—such as arrows, bolts, sling bullets, and other objects of comparable size—can't pass through the area. Passing through the area causes attacks with bigger ranged weapons, such as [thrown](/Traits.aspx?ID=195) weapons, to take a –2 circumstance penalty to their attack rolls if their paths pass through the emanation. Massive ranged weapons and spell effects that don't create physical objects can pass through the emanation with no penalty.
  • The area is difficult terrain to creatures attempting to move through it.
  • Gases, including creatures in gaseous form, can't pass through the emanation. When the emanation arises, such gases are removed from the area, including your space.
  • The area, including your space, has breathable air.
Once the magic is used, the ocarina remains a non-magical [virtuoso musical instrument](/Equipment.aspx?ID=37).

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Wind-Up Cart](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1120)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Clockwork" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=331" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Gadget" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=405" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 71

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) All Pathfinder Society agents have access to all uncommon clockwork items and gadgets from Chapters 1 and 2 of this book_

**Price** 6 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 2
</row>

**Access** Characters from Absalom, New Thassilon, Alkenstar, Dongun Hold, or especially technological regions of Arcadia like the Deadshot Lands have access to uncommon clockwork items from the first two chapters of this book. Due to the use of technology, all gadgets are uncommon or rare, though inventors and regions with access to inventors have access to uncommon gadgets.

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This primitive device can be cobbled together from springs, wheels, and scrap and is commonly used to carry rocks or other dead weight forward to trigger traps. It can be loaded with up to 4 Bulk of items. Most creatures aren't small enough to fit on the cart, and even for Tiny creatures, it makes for a choppy ride; while riding the cart, a creature gains two actions at the start of each of its turns, instead of three. Once activated, the cart moves forward at a speed of 30 feet per round on your turn for up to 1 minute. If it strikes an obstruction, it attempts to continue its movement, pushing with an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) bonus of +5, once per round. The wind-up cart has AC 15, Hardness 2, 24 Hit Points, and a Break Threshold of 12. After its 1-minute duration completes, the cart collapses back into scrap.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 3+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Wind-up Widget](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5244)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritence](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 104

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These simple constructs are often created for children or as proof of concept for larger tools. Despite their resemblance to clockworks, _wind-up widgets_ are animated by magic rather than complex internal mechanisms. They lack power sources, however, and must still be wound up before use. 

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 1 minute ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You turn the widget’s crank for 1 minute, and it comes to life. The widget operates autonomously—as described in its entry—for 10 minutes, then curls into a small metal ball until your next daily preparations.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
level="2"
right="Item 5"
pfs="Standard"
>
Wind-up Widget (Hand-powered Digger)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritence](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 104

**Price** 140 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 1

</row>

</column>

---

The _hand-powered digger_ resembles a small handheld drill. Once activated and placed against a surface, at the start of each of your turns, it digs 15 feet in a straight line through dirt, sand, or another loose material (as a burrow Speed) or deals 5 damage to any harder or denser material, ignoring that material’s Hardness if it’s 4 or less. The digger leaves a tunnel 1 foot in diameter behind it.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 4"
pfs="Standard"
>
Wind-up Widget (Thieves' Friend)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritence](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 105

**Price** 80 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 1

</row>

</column>

---

The _thieves’ friend_ resembles a small thieves’ toolkit with clockwork legs. Once activated, at the start of each of your turns, it moves up to 30 feet in a straight line toward the nearest locked object within 120 feet of it, then attempts to [Pick a Lock](/Actions.aspx?ID=2412) with a +10 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) modifier. The _thieves’ friend_ can detect locked objects [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) in mundane ways but not those [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) by magic.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Standard"
>
Wind-up Widget (Wind-up Spy)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritence](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 105

**Price** 50 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

The _wind-up spy_ resembles a small toy soldier in uniform. When activated, you choose a distance up to 80 feet, and the spy moves that far in a straight line. At the start of each of your turns, it records the next 6 seconds of sounds from within 25 feet, overwriting the previous 6 seconds. You can use a single action with the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) trait to have it save the current recording and walk the same distance backward, ending the activation early. You can Interact with the spy to play back its current recording.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 3+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Wind-up Wings](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1101)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Clockwork" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=331" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 65

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) All Pathfinder Society agents have access to all uncommon clockwork items and gadgets from Chapters 1 and 2 of this book_

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** attached to a thrown weapon

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These delicate clockwork wings enable thrown weapons to soar through the air at high speeds, performing turns and other aerial maneuvers midflight. Wind-up wings also have different types of special effects depending on the type. Wind-up wings must be attached to a [thrown](/Traits.aspx?ID=195) weapon and wound to function. A thrown weapon with an attached set of wind-up wings can't have anything else attached to it, or the wings cease to function.

 Attaching or detaching a pair of wind-up wings to a thrown weapon requires a [repair kit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=43), and the process takes 10 minutes. Winding an attached pair of wind-up wings takes three Interact actions. There are a variety of wind-up wings, with different effects.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Standard"
>
Wind-up Wings (Flutterback)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 65

**Price** 50 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

When you make a thrown Strike with the weapon to which a pair of flutterback wind-up wings are attached, and the wings are wound, the wings fly the weapon back to your hand after the Strike is complete. If your hands are full when the weapon returns, the wings hover in place three feet above the ground. At the end of your turn, the wings are wound down; they don't function again until wound. If you aren't holding the weapon when the flutterback wind-up wings become wound down, the weapon falls to the ground.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 12"
pfs="Standard"
>
Wind-up Wings (Homing)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 65

**Price** 1,800 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

When you make a thrown Strike with the weapon to which a pair of homing wind-up wings are attached, and the wings are wound, the wings seek out your target, flying through cover and avoiding obstacles. You ignore the target's [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) condition and reduce the target's cover by one step (lesser cover to no cover, standard cover to lesser cover, or greater cover to standard cover). After the Strike is complete, the wings are wound down; they don't function again until wound.

---

These magical platforms are used in a variety of performances. They allow performers to access high places safely, while also serving an important role before the performance even begins. They’re used by various backstage crews to hang lights, curtains, and scenery above the stage. Sometimes several of these platforms are lined up to make an upper and lower stage. This large 10-foot-by-10-foot platform can be secured to a surface as a 1-minute activity. While standing on a secured platform, any creature can use the Adjust Height activation.

**Activate—Adjust Height** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** The platform and all creatures and items on the platform either rise or lower up to 10 feet. This action fails if there is more than 50 Bulk on the platform.

</column>

    right="Item 7"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Winder's Ring](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1596)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Outlaws of Alkenstar</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #179: Cradle of Quartz](/Sources.aspx?ID=122) pg. 79

**Price** 360 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This ring contains dozens of minute, interlocking bronze gears that buzz incessantly. The ring grants you a +1 item bonus to all [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) checks to construct or repair clockworks.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> varies (Interact);     **Effect** The _winder's ring_ extends a winding key that fits any clockwork contraption or creature, allowing you to fully wind a clockwork device or creature in half the usual time. When you activate a _winder's ring_ in this way, attempt a DC 16 flat check. On a failure, the _winder's ring_ exhausts itself, and you can't activate it again until the next time you make your daily preparations.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The _winder's ring_ transforms into a [clockwork spy](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1095) that doesn't require winding and obeys your spoken commands for up to 1 hour. In this form, the _winder's ring_ has the [minion](/Traits.aspx?ID=109) trait. You can use this action again to return the clockwork spy to _winder's ring_ form as long as you're adjacent to the clockwork spy. If the clockwork spy is slain, it reverts to its ring shape, and the _winder's ring_ can't be activated again until 1 week has passed.

</column>

Carved of ash wood and decorated with images of clouds and gusting winds, a _windstep sheath_ is a small icon shaped like a weapon sheath or quiver. >
[Wine of the Blood](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1635)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Healing" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=89" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
<trait label="Potion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=130" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 114

**Price** 30 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This wine, prepared using the blood of a creature with overwhelming vitality, soothes the body, mind, and spirit with a temporary sense of euphoria and rest. When you drink _wine of the blood_, you recover 2d10 Hit Points. Additionally, the wine attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) every negative [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60) effect affecting you, with a counteract level of 3 and a counteract modifier of +9. Lastly, you gain a +1 status bonus to all Will saves, or a +2 status bonus against emotion effects, for 1 minute.

</column>

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** etched onto armor

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This rune is a swirling glyph on the front of the armor. A large pair of transparent, ephemeral wings floats out from the back of the armor. 

**Activate—Take to the Skies** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You trace the rune on the front of the breastplate, and the armor’s ephemeral wings grow tangible, granting you a [fly Speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=400) of 25 feet or your land Speed, whichever is slower. This effect lasts for 5 minutes or until you [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=74) it. Once the effect ends, the wings disappear completely, reappearing in their ephemeral form 1 hour later.

May contain spoilers from Spore War **Source** [Pathfinder #211: The Secret of Deathstalk Tower](/Sources.aspx?ID=254) pg. 82 **Price** 6,500 gp **Usage** held in 1+ hand(s) **Bulk** 1 **Base Weapon** [Composite Shortbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=435) --- This _[+2 greater striking ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [frost ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2839) [composite shortbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=435)_ belonged to a legendary scout, Jelarial, who found herself in command of a company of elves fleeing Mierani north into the Crown of the World to escape the doom of Earthfall thousands of years ago. Wintershot resurfaced during the war to reclaim Kyonin from Tanglebriar several thousand years later, wielded by a succession of mysterious snipers whose movements through the woodland confounded the demons, so much so that it gave rise to rumors that Jelarial’s ghost had returned to the south to aid her kin in a time of need. When making a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with _Wintershot_, targets do not gain [concealment](/Rules.aspx?ID=424) from the effects of mist or precipitation, and circumstance penalties to attacks of up to –2 imparted from [strong winds](/Rules.aspx?ID=2821) are negated. **Activate—Auroral Shine** ([cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [light](/Traits.aspx?ID=640), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) **Frequency** once per 10 minutes; **Effect** Fire an arrow at a target. If you hit, instead of dealing damage with the arrow, the creature struck must attempt a DC 34 Fortitude save. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is surrounded by shimmering lights akin to an aurora, causing it to become [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) for 2 rounds. If the creature was [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=83), it becomes [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) instead. If the creature was already concealed for any other reason, it is no longer concealed.
**Failure** As success, but the creature also takes 2d6 [persistent cold damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86), and the light affects the creature for 1 minute.
**Critical Failure** As success, but the creature also takes 4d6 persistent cold damage, and the light affects the creature for 10 minutes. **Activate—Signal Flare** ([light](/Traits.aspx?ID=640), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You pull back _Wintershot’s_ string and fire an arrow straight upward. The arrow soars to a height of 500 feet, or until it strikes a solid surface like a ceiling. When it reaches its apex, it explodes in a brilliant burst, creating a 100-foot radius area of bright light and dim light in the next 100 feet. In the night sky, this beacon can be seen clearly for miles. The beacon remains lit for up to 1 minute in a color of your choice. Alternately, you can fire a Signal Flare like a normal arrow to attempt to strike a Target—if it hits, the arrow inflicts normal damage and attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) one darkness effect of your choice that affects the area you hit with a counteract rank of 7th and a counteract modifier of +26.

May contain spoilers from Spore War **Source** [Pathfinder #212: A Voice in the Blight](/Sources.aspx?ID=255) pg. 73 **Usage** held in 1+ hand(s) **Bulk** 1 --- **Perception** +35; precise [low-light vision](/Rules.aspx?ID=2411) and hearing within 30 feet **Communication** [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=79) (partner only) **Skills** [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +33, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +35, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +35 **Int** +6, **Wis** +7, **Cha** +5 **Will** +35 --- The echo of the snowcaster Jelarial causes _Wintershot_ to become chill to the touch, yet despite feeling as cold as ice, she never causes harm or discomfort to her partner. Wintershot’s string issues a soft hissing sound, as of snow softly falling, and snowflakes drift down from the string and swiftly melt each time the bow is fired. _Wintershot’s_ voice is eager and excitable, often waxing poetic on a nearby object or creature of beauty or offering compliments to her partner. _Wintershot_ is a _[+3 major striking ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [greater frost ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2839) [holy ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2842) [composite shortbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=435)_. When making a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with _Wintershot_, targets don’t gain [concealment](/Rules.aspx?ID=424) from the effects of mist or [precipitation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2816), and circumstance penalties to attacks imparted from strong winds are negated. **Activate—Auroral Shine** ([cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [light](/Traits.aspx?ID=640)) **Frequency** once per minute; **Effect** _Wintershot_ can’t use this activation. When you activate Auroral Shine, fire an arrow at a target. If you hit, instead of dealing damage with the arrow, the creature struck must attempt a DC 43 Fortitude save. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is surrounded by shimmering lights akin to the aurora, causing it to become dazzled for 2 rounds. If the creature was [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=83), it becomes [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) instead. If the creature was already concealed for any other reason, it’s no longer concealed.
**Failure** As success, but the creature also takes 6d6 [persistent cold damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86), and the lights affect the creature for 1 minute.
**Critical Failure** As success, but the creature also takes 6d6 persistent cold damage, and the lights affect the creature for 10 minutes. **Activate—Signal Flare** ([light](/Traits.aspx?ID=640), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per hour; **Effect** _Wintershot_ fires an arrow-shaped construct of ice straight upward. The arrow soars to a height of 500 feet, or until it strikes a solid surface like a ceiling. When it reaches its apex, it explodes in a brilliant burst, creating a 100-foot radius area of [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2402) and [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2403) in the next 100 feet. In the night sky, this beacon can be seen clearly for miles. The beacon remains lit for up to 1 minute in a color of _Wintershot’s_ choice. Alternatively, _Wintershot_ can fire this Signal Flare like a normal arrow to attempt to [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) a target her partner can see—if it hits, the arrow inflicts normal damage and attempts to counteract one darkness effect of Wintershot’s choice that affects the creature struck, with a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) rank of 9th and a +25 modifier to the roll (+30 modifier if the source of the [darkness](/Traits.aspx?ID=569) effect was created by a [fiend](/Traits.aspx?ID=600)). **Activate—Rimecrust** ([cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631)) **Effect** _Wintershot_ causes the deep chill of winter to settle upon a single creature she can see or hear within 30 feet. That creature must attempt a DC 43 Fortitude save, after which point they’re temporarily immune to Rimecrust for 24 hours. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature’s discomfort and shivering from the sudden drop in temperature causes it to become [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the start of its next turn. Creatures that are [immune](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) to cold are immune to this effect.
**Failure** The creature becomes encrusted with ice. It becomes [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1 and [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) for 1 minute, or until it [Escapes](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) from the crusting ice (DC 43).
**Critical Failure** The creature is slowed 1 and [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90) by crusting ice until it Escapes (DC 43). After it Escapes, it remains slowed 1 and [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) for 1 minute from the lingering cold. _Nethys Note: the non-artifact version of the item is [here.](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3702) This artifact's heroic legacy, and its subsequent skills and ability attribute, are presented [here](/Rules.aspx?ID=3419). _

<title

    right="Item 9+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Wisp Chain](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2587)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Air" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=5" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 76

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn armor

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Armor** [Chain Shirt](/Armor.aspx?ID=6)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This _+1 [resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=279) [chain shirt](/Armor.aspx?ID=6)_ is made of small, interlocking currents of wind carefully woven together. While the links of air don't jingle against each other like chain links might, the tiny cyclones nevertheless create a blustering howl akin to standing at the center of a storm. A creature that ends its turn adjacent to you must attempt a DC 23 Fortitude save. On a failure, it becomes [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=8) until it moves away from you.

**Activate—Slicing Links** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You unbind the currents that form your armor and release them as cutting whorls of air that slice into creatures in a 60-foot cone. Creatures in the area take 6d6 slashing damage with a DC 25 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save. A creature that fails its save is also [pushed](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) 10 feet (or 20 feet on a critical failure). You lose the AC bonus of your armor until the end of your turn, when the air currents reform the wisp chain around you.

</column>

---

This _+1 [resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=279) [chain shirt](/Armor.aspx?ID=6)_ is made of small, interlocking currents of wind carefully woven together. While the links of air don't jingle against each other like chain links might, the tiny cyclones nevertheless create a blustering howl akin to standing at the center of a storm. A creature that ends its turn adjacent to you must attempt a DC 23 Fortitude save. On a failure, it becomes [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=8) until it moves away from you.

**Activate—Slicing Links** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You unbind the currents that form your armor and release them as cutting whorls of air that slice into creatures in a 60-foot cone. Creatures in the area take 6d6 slashing damage with a DC 25 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save. A creature that fails its save is also [pushed](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) 10 feet (or 20 feet on a critical failure). You lose the AC bonus of your armor until the end of your turn, when the air currents reform the wisp chain around you.

    right="Item 3"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Witch's Finger](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1935)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 51

**Price** 11 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Shaped like a pointed, gnarled finger on a stick, witch's finger is a frozen treat imbued with berries that lend it a blood-red hue. A popular tale claims Irriseni winter witches created this dessert, but the story is apocryphal; an enterprising ice cream shop owner in New Stetven invented the treat and, as a marketing ploy, the myth surrounding it. Taking a bite makes you feel warm. For 1 hour, you have cold resistance 3, and for 8 hours, the treat negates the damage you would take from [severe environmental cold](/Rules.aspx?ID=642) and reduces the damage you take from extreme cold to that of severe cold.

</column>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Catalyst" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=791" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=564" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 119

**Price** 52 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><row>[Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) (add 1 action)</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The pelt of a [witchwarg](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3231) stays cold long after it leaves the creature's body. A tuft of this fur can freeze a [_fire shield_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1529) spell into solid ice, inverting its usual effects. The spell's [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) trait is replaced with the [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555) trait, you gain [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) to fire damage and [environmental heat effects](/Rules.aspx?ID=2820) (instead of cold effects), the shield is immune to cold damage instead of fire damage, and its [Hardness](/Rules.aspx?ID=2183) is halved against fire effects. The damage you deal to creatures that touch you or hit you with a melee or unarmed attack has its type changed to cold.

</column>

    level="1"
    right="Item 17"
    pfs=""
>
[Witchwyrd Beacon](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2500)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Stolen Fate</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #191: The Destiny War](/Sources.aspx?ID=199) pg. 71

**Price** 15,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 3
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Made of [djezet](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1410), [orichalcum](/Equipment.aspx?ID=276), and luminous, resonant crystal, a _witchwyrd beacon_ looks like a series of concentric rings mounted on rods that allow the rings to rotate independently of each other. These potent items are used by the Pactmasters of Katapesh to facilitate swift travel and are only rarely entrusted to others.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes (command, envision, Interact);     **Effect** By touching the _witchwyrd beacon_ and focusing on it for 10 minutes, you attune yourself to it. Up to four creatures can be attuned to a single _witchwyrd beacon_ at any one time—to attune another creature, one of the previous four must become unattuned. You can break your attunement to a _witchwyrd beacon_ by Dismissing the effect. The attunement automatically ends if the attuned creature dies or if the attuned creature attunes themselves to a different _witchwyrd beacon_. The effect can also be dispelled normally. You can sense whenever the _witchwyrd beacon_ you are attuned to is activated in any way.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes (command, Interact);  **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** you are attuned to the _witchwyrd beacon_; **Effect** You place the _witchwyrd beacon_ on a flat, stable, and immobile surface, then adjust its rings to link it to the site. Once linked, any creature can use a [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=156) effect to target the _witchwyrd beacon_ directly, regardless of line of sight. You can [_dimension door_](/Spells.aspx?ID=69) or [_gate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=130) to the beacon as if you could see its location, and if you travel to it via an effect like [_plane shift_](/Spells.aspx?ID=222), the beacon eliminates the imprecision of the spell. The beacon doesn't change the range of effects, only their accuracy. Once the beacon is used in this manner, it loses its link and must be reactivated again to grant this benefit to attuned creatures.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

A _wizard's tower_ is a tiny gaming piece carved into the form of a stone tower.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes (command, envision, Interact);     **Effect** The gaming piece transforms into a fully furnished stone tower 80 feet high and 30 feet in diameter. The tower is topped by a peaked wooden roof, with a wooden door on the second floor accessed by wooden stairs on the tower's exterior. A spiral staircase in the center of the tower connects its 6 floors. The bottom floor is empty, ideal for storage, and the second floor is a great hall for audiences and guests. The third and fourth floors are divided into servants quarters and guest rooms, while the top two floors feature luxurious personal chambers and an alchemy lab. You can revert the tower back to its original state by climbing to the top floor and using an action to speak a command word.

<column gap="tiny">

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

---

[Barbarians](/Classes.aspx?ID=2), [druids](/Classes.aspx?ID=6) and other outlanders are often forced to spend the harsh winter months protecting their communities from one of the deadliest predators to stalk the forests and taiga of the northern reaches, the fearsome [witchwargs](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3231). This _+1 [hide armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=7)_ is assembled from the hide and fur of a trio of witchwargs, and it conveys on the wearer both an attack akin to the witchwargs' deadly jaws and the ability to channel the frigid cold of the witchwargs's Winter Breath.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You breathe a cloud of frost in a 15-foot cone that deals 5d8 cold damage (DC 23 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save).

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You gain a jaws unarmed attack that you make using your hands. This attack deals 1d8 piercing damage plus 1 cold damage, is in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) group, and has the [trip](/Traits.aspx?ID=196) and [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) traits.

**Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include the hides of at least three [witchwargs](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3231).

</column>
